title: Burst allocation timebase drift during Private->Dedicated switchover causing opaque throttles
creator: Asha Patel
description: During an automated switchover from Private to Dedicated routing for a large tenant, a drift between two allocation timebases caused burst credits to be misapplied. The orchestrator and admission proxies used different epoch anchors for burst ledger reconciliation, which resulted in immediate silent 429 rejections and opaque errors for customer traffic for ~14 minutes. This ticket captures the investigation, mitigation, and long-term fix plan.
reproduction_steps:
1) Configure tenant in Private mode with reserved burst budget.
2) Trigger a controlled switchover to Dedicated routing (simulated in staging).
3) Force orchestrator snapshot + fast follower restart where system clocks are slightly skewed (simulate NTP jitter).
4) Replay high QPS traffic spikes for 2 minutes using the tenant's traffic profile.
Expected: smooth handoff of burst ledger. Observed: admission proxies reject requests with 429 and 'quota_unavailable' until manual resync.

mitigations: Increased admission controller grace window from 2s -> 60s for switchover transactions (hotfix).
Forced orchestrator->proxy ledger reconciliation (control plane command).
Notified affected customer and provided summary + credits.
root_cause: Two components used different timebase anchors for ledger epochs during snapshot-based handoff. A follower node experienced transient clock drift (NTP jitter) which changed its local epoch anchor; when the orchestrator applied a snapshot the proxy validated credits against its stale timebase and treated the ledger as inconsistent, causing opaque quota rejections. There was no explicit epoch versioning or monotonicity guard between components.
fix_summary: 1) Add explicit epoch UUID and monotonic counter to ledger snapshots so proxies can detect stale anchors instead of failing closed. 2) Switch admission checks to use monotonic timebase derived from orchestrator leader's epoch (fall back to snapshot UUID). 3) Improve switchover choreography to include handshake ACKs and a safe-apply window. 4) Add integration test that injects NTP jitter and validates no 429s during switchover.
rollout_plan: Stage patch to staging cluster and run the switchover+chaos test suite (48h). If green, canary to two non-critical Dedicated pools for 6h, then ramp to all Dedicated pools over 24h. For Private customers we will push the patch via Private control-plane update and coordinate a maintenance window for on-prem customers.

qa_tests:
- End-to-end switchover test with synthetic traffic and injected clock jitter.
- Unit tests for snapshot UUID parsing and monotonic counter semantics.
- Load test verifying admission latency/throughput unchanged after change.
notes: During the incident the emergency hotfix (grace window increase) prevented wider impact but masked a deeper compatibility gap. We correlated the failure to a follower node that had a recent kernel NTP bug; we should coordinate with infra about stricter NTP monitoring on control plane nodes. The fix is backward-compatible: proxies that don't understand epoch UUID will fallback to timestamp heuristic for one rollout cycle, but we will require full upgrade for long-term safety.
